thesis: The bear carries the current-price objection because comparable-demand quality does not demonstrate owner-cash value at 44.49x vendor earnings. Annual growth survives tariff normalisation, so a business-decline sell thesis is unsupported. Normalised membership economics and cash valuation are required for a stronger purchase ruling.
strongest_counterexample: Annual net sales grew 10.1%, earnings increased to $9.226bn from $8.099bn and adjusted comparables rose 6.6%; these establish genuine operating progress independent of the $0.15 quarterly refund.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable annual adjusted comparable-sales growth rate at or below zero would invalidate the retained demand-duration premise.

A matched primary cash/debt and membership-earnings bridge shows positive normalised earnings growth and post-investment/service cash above zero, resolving the central owner-cash gap and requiring entry-value reassessment.
evidence_gaps: Debt, FCF and normalised membership economics.
Owner-cash valuation and persistence of comparable growth.
Durable recovery rather than an overbought low-volume rebound.
decisive_factors: 44.49x vendor reference is not demonstrated fair value.
Net-income/net-sales denominator excludes membership fees; price below SMA-200.
